The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
super(core, updateHandler.getUpdateLog());
this.ulog != null && this.ulog == existingLog
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when the `SolrCore` is reloaded, the existing `UpdateLog` is reused without properly notifying it of the change in the update handler. This can lead to the `UpdateLog` using stale or incorrect data during update operations, as it is not initialized correctly after the core reload.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
if (this.ulog != null && this.ulog == existingLog) {
    this.ulog.init(this, core);
}
```
Reason:
The fix involves checking if the existing `UpdateLog` is being reused and then explicitly calling the `init` method on it. This ensures that the `UpdateLog` is properly informed of the update handler's change, allowing it to initialize correctly and avoid inconsistencies during update operations after the core reload.
